clue.text: Job description

parts.note: reads as an employment term, but Job is the Old Testament figure famed for his endless forbearance under suffering

explanation.surface: A dry phrase from a personnel office about what a role involves.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital J is hidden at the start of the clue: this is the biblical Job, proverbial for enduring his trials without complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial 'patience of Job' makes the adjective a fair one-word portrait of the biblical sufferer.

clue.text: Springer regularly does it in a sticky situation

definitions.text: Springer regularly does it in a sticky situation

parts.words: Springer regularly does it in a sticky situation
parts.note: a bouncer on a spring-loaded stick does this repeatedly; sticky is literal, not awkward

explanation.surface: A spaniel or a talk-show host regularly getting into a jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouncing on a spring-loaded stick, or the punk dance imitating it, is jumping in a sticky way.

clue.text: In college upset your old man

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the college's letters upside down

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
thy is the archaic your

explanation.surface: Your father is distressed at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your old man' wants to be a father, but only 'man' defines; your and old give THY and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so the definition 'man' covers it by example.

clue.text: Scary country, Spain after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution things are turned round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A frightening nation, with Spain following an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is spooky and unsettling, a near synonym of scary.

clue.text: Entertainer? Time stripper got topless!

indicators.note: topless means the stripper loses her first letter

parts.note: a lap dancer is a kind of stripper

explanation.surface: Showtime: the exotic dancer removed her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' means losing the top letter, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofer in metal-tipped shoes performs on stage, so is one kind of entertainer, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fish's journey across rough water

indicators.note: the journey stretches across the fish, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a journey is a trip
the ide is a freshwater fish, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A salmon's long migration through choppy seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong current where tides meet gives choppy, turbulent sea, so the phrase names rough water.

clue.text: Well in credit, Henry invested

indicators.note: invested means put in, so Henry's letter goes inside credit

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry put money into a bank account that is healthily in the black.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thick with someone is being close friends, as is being well in with them.

clue.text: Alarmed half of Tory ladies, I fancy, including these?

definitions.text: Alarmed half of Tory ladies, I fancy, including these?

indicators.note: fancy as a verb, imagine, but as adjective it means elaborate, signalling a rearrangement
half of takes the back two of the four letters of Tory

explanation.surface: Some Conservative women are perturbed, and the setter guesses they read a certain paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Alarmed, RY, ladies and I are shuffled into the newspaper's name; the whole clue describes the stereotypical, easily alarmed readership.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's Daily Mail is a right-leaning tabloid known for alarmist headlines, its readership often caricatured as alarmed Tory ladies.

clue.text: See 6
Argued case for penny on petrol, sort of

indicators.note: in a down clue the penny comes on top of the petrol

parts.note: leaded is a type of petrol, now banned

explanation.surface: Someone made the case for a penny extra on fuel duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleading is arguing a case in court, so the past tense is argued a case.

clue.text: Sweet face about to fall

indicators.note: about signals turning the word for face round

parts.note: mug is slang for face
to drop is to fall

explanation.surface: Someone's smiling expression is about to collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy jelly confection is a kind of sweet, the British word for candy.

clue.text: Do like it when current partner's around

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: the partner goes around the word it, holding it inside

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Copy it whenever your spouse is nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To do like someone is to copy them, an everyday sense of mimicry.

clue.text: Where old conservationist was keeping department ignorant

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, here the department letter

parts.note: Noah, who saved the animals from the Flood, was in the ark

explanation.surface: A historical environmentalist withheld information from a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old conservationist' is Noah, who preserved every species aboard his ark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept uninformed is the idiom of having no light on a matter, hence ignorant.

clue.text: Why I 'ad to return

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y
with the H dropped Cockney-style, had becomes 'ad; its synonym held, dropped the same way, gives 'eld

explanation.surface: A Cockney asking why he had to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'ad tells you to drop it from the synonym too: held without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment's yield is its return, and as verbs both mean produce a profit.

clue.text: Chap my boss made fun of

parts.note: a guy is a chap
for a journalist the boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: A man whose employer mocked him.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is an old verb for ridiculing them, from effigies of Guy Fawkes.

clue.text: His doesn't work — it's bent

indicators.note: work, as in work dough, means knead into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's broken device that has buckled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for crooked or corrupt, as in a bent copper.

clue.text: Surveyed scans A&E produced over 5d

indicators.note: produced in the sense of made up or concocted signals rearranging the letters

parts.note: the letters of scans plus A and E from the ampersand phrase
read as five old pence: V is the Roman numeral five and d the old penny

explanation.surface: A hospital emergency department's scan results, costing a trifling sum, have been reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: '5d' pretends to point to clue 5 down, but it is just five and d, V and D, joining the anagram. A&E is the UK hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvassed opinion has been sounded out, a synonym of surveyed, as in a poll.

clue.text: Can one settle comfortably outside city?

indicators.note: outside means the settling goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to nestle is to settle cosily
can is slang for a toilet, a WC
A means one

explanation.surface: A question of whether anyone could make a cosy home on the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcastle upon Tyne is a major city in north-east England.

clue.text: Raises environment finally with Green politician

parts.note: jacks, as in jacks up a car, means raises

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of environment

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner from the Green Party lifts environmental issues.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw is a former British Labour Home and Foreign Secretary; 'Green' is not his party but an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a well-known British Labour minister, so an example of a politician.

clue.text: Island's very good on the surface — stick around!

parts.note: to jam is to stick fast
A1, very good, looks like the letters AI on the surface
ca, circa, means around

explanation.surface: An island looking great from the outside invites you to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 written down looks like AI, so 'on the surface' means judged by appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica is a Caribbean island nation, so a direct example.

clue.text: Conservative strongly backing demand

parts.note: all for means wholeheartedly in favour

explanation.surface: A Tory vigorously supporting an ultimatum.
explanation.definitionFit: To call for something is to demand it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Readily accept return of an immature creature

indicators.note: return asks for the adjective to be read the other way round

parts.note: pupal describes the pupa, the immature stage of an insect

explanation.surface: Eagerly welcoming back a young animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up praise or a story is to accept it eagerly, the idiom of a cat drinking milk.

clue.text: Not requiring payment for singer

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
Bono is the U2 frontman

explanation.surface: A rock star who performs for free.
explanation.walkthrough: Bono is famous for unpaid campaigning, so the pairing is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for the public good, used for professional work done free of charge.

clue.text: Priest and sweetheart like sexy underwear in church office

indicators.note: heart takes the middle letter of sweet

parts.note: lacy describes lingerie

explanation.surface: A cleric and his lover dressed in risqué lingerie inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The post of a prelate, a bishop or similar, is a senior ecclesiastical office.

clue.text: Doctor's onto sickness in French port

indicators.note: the doctor is placed onto, that is after, the sickness

parts.note: mal is French for illness
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's journey to a French harbour town where illness has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French port' looks like the definition, but French belongs to the wordplay; the port is Swedish.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmö is a major Swedish harbour city on the Öresund strait, so an example of a port.

clue.text: Minder — Terry initially absent from start of story

indicators.note: absent from means a letter is missing from the opening section

parts.note: a book's story starts with chapter one

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of Terry

explanation.surface: A babysitter called Terry is missing from the opening of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone supervises young people, especially a young woman, so is a minder.

clue.text: Speaking with sense is commended

indicators.note: speaking means the word is to be pronounced, giving one with the same sound

parts.note: sighted means having the sense of sight

explanation.surface: Talking sensibly is praiseworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier cited in dispatches is officially praised for bravery, so mentioned with commendation.

clue.text: System meant to hold up West Country tourist

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from bottom to top, reversing the letters
the two words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A scheme intended to delay a holidaymaker in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; Cornish locals call a tourist an emmet, an old word for ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornish dialect uses this old word for ant as a disparaging name for visitors.

clue.text: Provided car with wing missing — dodgy in the extreme

parts.note: if means provided that

indicators.note: the car loses an end, as a car might lose a wing

parts.note: the Ford Fiesta is a popular car

explanation.surface: A supplied car missing a wing looks very suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is British slang for dubious; its superlative means most dubious.

clue.text: Game Boy's a throwback

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name
a followed by lob, a throw, all read backwards

explanation.surface: A lad's video game console is outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game Boy' is a red herring: it reads as Nintendo's console but splits into the definition and Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle-style lottery drawn from a revolving drum, a game of chance at fêtes.

clue.text: A scolded bishop ignored bubbly

indicators.note: ignored means the bishop's letter is left out

parts.note: berated means scolded
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric told off a bishop who paid no attention to the champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerated liquid has air or gas forced through it, making it fizzy like champagne.

clue.text: Opening with work in disorder

indicators.note: in places the work inside the opening

parts.note: an entry is an opening, a way in
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A first night with a piece of music that descends into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and in loose usage, entropy is a measure of randomness, hence disorder.
